parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime is dominated by the parent nation. Every visitor passes a national entry screen where a February 2025 cable directs officers to refuse cases with document/record sex discrepancies and to weigh permanent lifetime fraud ineligibility for suspected misrepresentation — a universal-exposure lever with documented detentions of foreign nationals. A rider attaches a facilities ban to this jurisdiction itself; its scope and enforcement beyond the December 2024 activist arrests are unsourced. National custody records document severe abuse of trans detainees (conversion-style policies, forced labour, sexual abuse), a tier-1 exposure contingent on detention. Local evidence is mildly favourable — no local bathroom ban, a 2026 low-risk placement — but explicitly reversible by national override, so it cannot lift the score materially. No execution pathway is documented; typical harms are refusal, humiliating screening, and denial rather than imprisonment. The regime sits in the Elevated Risk band, near the 0.45 anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: Passport policy bars self-selected/X markers; officers instructed to refuse on sex discrepancies and consider lifetime fraud findings; trans athletes barred; foreign citizens detained over visa issues; travellers report confiscation/stranding.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; foreign-issued documents normally govern, and the fraud finding requires all four elements with limited waiver.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy at visa or entry can escalate to refusal, investigation, and detention; a lifetime ineligibility finding forecloses future travel.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau mandates haircut/hormone-withdrawal policies for trans inmates; immigration custody documented with forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans detainees.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any entry dispute or minor offence routing a visitor into national custody or immigration detention exposes them to birth-sex placement and documented abuse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: A national legislature rider imposes a facilities restriction on this jurisdiction itself; scope and enforcement beyond the December 2024 arrests unsourced; nationwide, bans cover government buildings in ~21 jurisdictions and criminal trespass in 4, with a documented handcuffed arrest.
federal_state_facilities.protection: The jurisdiction has no bathroom ban of its own; 29 states plus the capital district have none in mapped categories.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National facilities in the district follow the parent rule regardless of local law; the visitor cannot rely on the local council to repeal the rider.

care_services.exposure: Visitor-facing care restriction not documented for adults here; proposed national rules would bar reimbursement for under-18 care, and hospitals received subpoenas for minors' records.
care_services.interaction: An adult's care needs appear low-exposure; a minor's care-seeking could trigger records exposure under national investigations.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive orders frame gender-affirming care as 'mutilation'; DOJ memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'; 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; advocacy groups compare to genocide — state threat-framing raising hostility and outing probability.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism powers are stated not to target mere disagreement; orders partly blocked or enjoined in court.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Framing is directed at advocacy/speech; it colours police and institutional climate rather than creating a direct criminal charge for a visitor.

minors_guardians.exposure: Care for minors banned in 27 states; proposed national reimbursement bar; EO directs criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating a minor's social transition; subpoena of hospitals for minors' records.
minors_guardians.interaction: A trans minor travelling with a guardian faces school/teacher scrutiny, records exposure, and no care continuity guarantee; the guardian's facilitation could be construed under the school EO.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Not documented at jurisdiction level; national hate-crime data covers sexual orientation broadly, not trans-specific visitor violence.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; employment discrimination barred under 2020 ruling — climate signals only.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local police practice and custody conditions in the jurisdiction are unsourced and unresolved, not evidence of safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Rider ban scope, local police practice, and local custody conditions unsourced; favourable rules can be overridden by the national legislature or executive without local change.
remedies_unknowns.protection: A legal-aid FAQ tracks passport rules; litigation challenges several measures; a July 2026 risk assessment places the jurisdiction on its low-risk list — though its method is unverifiable and it warns the reputation is no longer settled.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Open questions about documents at entry and detention placement remain unanswered; injunctions could shift operative rules at any time.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.45-D registers every visitor into databases exposing them durably, with harassment and eviction typical and imprisonment uncommon. The parent regime similarly imposes universal exposure via entry screening and the fraud cable, with refusal and detention rather than imprisonment the documented outcomes. Severity is comparable, but documented custodial abuse here is worse than 0.45-D's harassment tier; 0.45-D therefore sits near this rating, slightly above on custody.

0.35-A bars noncompliant trans visitors at the border routinely and without remedy. Here the fraud cable is discretionary — refusal requires a discrepancy or reasonable doubt, not automatic application — and existing X passports still work. Less universal than 0.35-A's register, but detentions of foreign nationals and the athlete ban narrow the gap; this rating sits above 0.35-A on frequency.

0.55-B features extended secondary screening with discretionary refusal, humiliation and delay but administrative consequences only. The parent's entry friction resembles it, but the fraud ineligibility lever, documented custody abuse, state threat-framing, and a facilities rider in the jurisdiction itself push severity below 0.55-B; this rating sits under it accordingly.

0.25-C's worst feature is birth-sex prison placement with frequent assaults plus criminalised cross-dressing in administrative buildings. The parent documents comparable or worse custody abuses (sexual abuse, conversion-style policies), but criminalisation of presentation is absent nationally and the typical visitor outcome is refusal, not custody. Well above 0.25-C on frequency and criminal exposure.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller's operative experience is almost entirely national: the entry screen (passport markers, fraud cable, discretionary refusals and detentions of foreign nationals) is unavoidable and universal; the rider-imposed facilities ban means even this locally unprotected jurisdiction carries an active restriction the local council cannot repeal; and documented national custody abuse forms a severe contingent exposure if any dispute escalates to detention. Local evidence — no own ban, low-risk placement, elected local government — is genuinely mitigating but fragile and explicitly reversible, so per the override rule the territory adds its own hostile layer (the rider) and cannot exceed the parent's operative average. No execution pathway is documented; worst credible outcomes are refusal, stranding, humiliating screening, facilities exclusion and, in custody, severe abuse. Minors add criminalised-facilitation and records-subpoena exposure. Net placement: Elevated Risk band, near the 0.45 anchors.
